tasks.short: Study the drawing, look up speeds and feeds, calculate the size and position of cuts and offsets, adjust after the first cut and save proven values.

steps.what: CNC operator studies the drawing for dimensions and material
CNC operator calculates machine speed and feed ratios from the tool maker's tables
CNC operator calculates the size and position of cuts and tool offsets
CNC operator adjusts speeds and feeds after the first cut
CNC operator notes proven values in a notebook for repeat jobs

tasks.design: The CAM tool library ({OTHER}) computes speeds and feeds from tool and material data, and the CAM model gives cut sizes, positions and offsets; the operator checks them. Proven values are saved with the program, so repeat jobs start from them. Adjusting after the first cut stays with the operator; no learning model sets values.
tasks.previous_blocker: Values were looked up in printed tables and worked out by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: CAM tool libraries hold cutting data per tool and material.
tasks.still_hard: Hard or unusual materials still need trial cuts.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing chatter and dropping the feed before the tool breaks.
tasks.altitude: The operator checks computed values instead of working them out.

reach.learn: Whether shared proven values improve programs.

evidence.claim: CAM tool libraries compute speeds and feeds from tool and material data.
Learning models in safety functions of machinery need third-party conformity assessment; this design keeps them out.

assumptions: Boundary: from the work order to saved settings; programming is outside.
Input contract: tool data from tool makers; material data from the ERP; fallback is printed tables.

Studying the drawing and adjusting after the first cut keep their full time. s2 keeps 30 and s3 keeps 40 for checking the computed values; s5 keeps 40 because saving the proven program is quick and the operator still notes what was changed and why.
The tool library is kept current.

already_counted.description: CNC operator checks computed speeds and feeds.
CNC operator checks computed cut positions.

incremental.description: CNC operator updates tool data when new tools arrive.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many jobs are in hard or unusual materials without library data, so values are still worked out from tables (22.5); high: tool and material data complete as assumed (37.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find the right program on the server, transfer it to the machine, check the version, run the simulation or dry run and save edits back to the server.

steps.what: CNC operator finds the right program version on the server
CNC operator transfers the program to the machine's control: on a USB stick today; over the network after the change, with older controls still taking a stick
CNC operator checks the loaded program matches the work order revision: by eye today; after the change the system checks it, and the operator checks only on older controls
CNC operator runs the simulation or a dry run before cutting
CNC operator checks the edits before sending: what changed in the program and why, written in a note for the programmer
CNC operator sends the checked edited program back to the server: on a stick today, over the network to the programmer's approval queue after the change

tasks.design: A program distribution system ({OTHER}) links the machine to the server over the network: choosing the work order at the machine loads the released program, and the system checks the revision against the work order before the program can run. The operator checks each edited program, notes the change and sends it once back to the server, flagged for the programmer's approval. Simulation or a dry run stays with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Programs were carried on USB sticks and versions checked by eye.
tasks.enabler_now: Program distribution systems connect CNC controls to servers with version control.
tasks.still_hard: Older controls without a network port still need a stick.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting in the dry run that a clamp sits in the tool path.

reach.learn: Whether flagged edits improve released programs.

evidence.claim: Program distribution systems connect CNC controls to servers and check program versions.
Per-operator logs in shop-floor systems can monitor staff and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the work order to saved edits; programming is outside.
Input contract: programs released by the CNC programmer; fallback is USB sticks.

Simulation, dry runs and the check of edits keep their full time. s1 keeps 30 for choosing the order and reading the loaded program; s2 and s3 keep 15 for older controls without a network port; s5 keeps 50 for sending and answering the programmer.
Programmers' time is outside the operator's savings.

approvals.approved_version: The edited program with the operator's change note exactly as checked in s5b, sent once to the programmer's approval queue on the server; any further edit needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of the controls are older ones without a network port, so sticks and eye checks stay for them (42.2); high: most controls networked (60.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Watch coolant flow at the cutting zone, check coolant concentration, top up coolant and lubricant and log the checks.

steps.what: CNC operator checks that workpieces are properly lubricated and cooled during machine operation
CNC operator measures coolant concentration with a refractometer
CNC operator tops up coolant and lubricant
CNC operator logs coolant checks: on the machine sheet today; after the change the sensor logs its readings and the operator enters the hand readings still taken

tasks.design: An inline sensor in the coolant tank shows concentration and level on the machine panel ({OPS_SYSTEM}) and logs them, so fewer refractometer checks and no paper log are needed. Watching coolant at the cutting zone and topping up stay with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Concentration was measured by hand and written on a sheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Inline coolant sensors report concentration and level.
tasks.still_hard: Sensors drift; a hand check is still needed now and then.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing smoke at the cut before the panel shows anything.

reach.learn: Whether logged concentration extends coolant life.

evidence.claim: Inline coolant sensors report concentration and level to the machine panel.
Machine logs tied to operators can monitor staff and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the running machine to the coolant log; coolant replacement is outside.
Input contract: sensor readings from the tank; limits set by the maintenance technician; fallback is the refractometer.
Watching and topping up keep their full time. s2 keeps 50 because sensors drift and hand checks stay for half of the readings; s4 keeps 40 for logging those hand readings.

incremental.description: CNC operator checks the sensor against a hand reading weekly.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: sensors drift often, so most hand checks and their logging stay (5.5); high: sensors hold their calibration as assumed (15.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Watch and listen to the machine, compare panel readings with specifications, measure parts for drift and report malfunctions to maintenance.

steps.what: CNC operator monitors machine operation by watching and listening
CNC operator compares control panel readings to specifications to detect malfunctions
CNC operator measures parts to check for drift
CNC operator writes the fault report for maintenance: on a paper note today; on the terminal with the alarm data attached after the change
CNC operator checks the fault report before it goes: machine, alarm data and the fault as seen and heard
CNC operator sends the checked fault report to maintenance

tasks.design: Spindle load, temperatures and vibration limits are set in the machine monitoring ({OPS_SYSTEM}), which alarms when a reading leaves its range, so the operator checks alarms instead of reading every value. The operator writes a fault report on the terminal with the alarm data attached, checks it and sends it once to maintenance. Watching, listening and measuring stay with the operator; limits are fixed rules, not a learning model.
tasks.previous_blocker: Panel values were read and compared by eye, and faults reported on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Machine monitoring sets limits and alarms on control data.
tasks.still_hard: Many faults show by sound or smell before any reading moves.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing a bearing start to whine.

evidence.claim: Machine monitoring sets limits on control data and raises alarms.
Per-operator logs in shop-floor systems need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the running machine to the fault report; repair is outside.
Input contract: limits set by the maintenance technician; fallback is reading the panel.

Watching, listening, measuring, the report check and the send keep their full time. s2 keeps 50 because alarms replace reading every value; s4 keeps 70 because the alarm data attach and the fault is still described by the operator.
Alarms are per machine, not per operator.

incremental.description: CNC operator reports false alarms so limits can be tuned.

approvals.approved_version: The fault report with machine, alarm data and the operator's description exactly as checked in s4b, sent once to maintenance from the terminal; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many faults show by sound or smell before any reading moves, so panel checks and written reports stay (6.5); high: limits catch most faults (14.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The CNC operator keeps adjusting, proving programs and watching the cut; tables, USB sticks, paper logs and reading every value shrink.
skills_to_grow: Working with program distribution and alarms
role.ambitious_version: An operator who runs more machines because routine checks come to them.
